actions: ran same-budget synthetic uncertainty-targeted probing ablation
compared no-probe, fixed epsilon=.05, targeted .05 boundary-crossing probes, and oracle64 over six evaluator regimes with 150 paired seeds
checked fresh public cost-aware observation and variable-feedback-precision evidence
persisted reproduction script and follow-up checkpoint

result_summary.main_result: At a nominal 5% probe rate, uncertainty-targeted boundary-crossing probes used slightly fewer probes and reduced the oracle-relative routing-regret proxy versus fixed epsilon in all three asymmetric evaluator regimes, but did not establish a reliable endpoint archive-quality advantage over fixed epsilon or no-probe learning; all targeted-vs-fixed paired 95% intervals included zero.
result_summary.negative_result: Raw decision-boundary uncertainty is not sufficient as the probing objective under a fixed evaluator-call budget.
result_summary.next_hypothesis: Price opportunity-model probes by expected future routing-regret reduction minus immediate lost B-EVSI, displaced proposal value, and controller cost.

exact_next_action: On next invocation resolve the then-current control tuple first, then implement a myopic value-of-information probe controller on the same synthetic family and compare it with target05, epsilon=.05, and no-probe using a pre-materialized common-randomness stream; report endpoint quality, B/probe calls, oracle64 routing regret, rare-state calibration, and horizon-multiplier sensitivity.
